title: O Blessed Souls Are They
description: O Blessed Souls Are They in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 32, part 1, headed “Forgiveness of sins upon confession”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O bless-ed souls are they Whose sins are cov-er'd o'er! Di-vine-ly blest, to whom the Lord im-putes their guilt no more.

lines: Divinely blest, to whom the Lord
And keep their hearts with care;
Their lips and lives without deceit,
Till I confess'd my sins to thee,
Let saints keep near the throne;
Our help in times of deep distress,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
